---
title: Show how a whole divides into parts you can count
description: A waffle gives every category the squares its share earns, so a share reads as a count of squares.
version: 0.0.1
styles: [scientific]
---

## Most trips are still made by car

These illustrative counts come from a commuter survey. The chart shares 100 squares out by the largest remainder method, so the squares always add up to the whole.

```chart
type: waffle
title: Cars carry four in ten trips
subtitle: Each square is 1% of the trips
data:
  inline:
    - {mode: Car, trips: 412}
    - {mode: Train, trips: 236}
    - {mode: Bicycle, trips: 118}
    - {mode: Walking, trips: 97}
    - {mode: Bus, trips: 61}
encoding: {x: mode, y: trips}
axes:
  y: {label: Trips}
```

*Source: Illustrative values.*

Use the keyboard or pointer to read each mode's trips, share and squares.
